info.description: Buyer and merchant-facing APIs for the Vimas e-commerce backend. Run "Register" (username + password, optionally referred_username) to create an account and auto-populate {{token}} and {{refresh_token}} — no email verification is required. Afterwards call "Update Profile" to add first/last name, email, address, country, and phone number. Use "Login (Username)" to sign back in, or "Refresh Token" once the access token expires.

request.description: type=reseller restricts results to bulk-purchasable products (bulk_available = 1); type=consumer to consumer-available products (consumer_available = 1); type=partner to partner-available products (partner_available = 1). Omit (or any other value) to get the full catalog. Points display: for consumer/default, each product includes totalPoints (if the product's showTotalPoints is on) and pointsSharing (if showPointsSharing is on) sourced from the product itself. For type=reseller, those same two fields instead come from EACH active bulk package under the product — returned as bulkPointsSharing: an array of { productBulkDetailsId, packageQuantity, totalPoints?, pointsSharing? }, one entry per package, each gated by that package's own showTotalPoints/showPointsSharing.

request.description: cart_type is optional and defaults to "consumer" (consumer | reseller | partner). consumer and reseller are separate rows for the same product — adding a reseller line for a product you already have as consumer creates a second row instead of merging quantities (a buyer can hold both at once). quantity is checked against consumerMinimumQuantity/consumerMaximumQuantity, resellerMinimumQuantity/resellerMaximumQuantity, or partnerMinimumQuantity/partnerMaximumQuantity depending on cart_type — 400 if outside those bounds. For cart_type="reseller", productBulkDetailsId is required — see the "Add To Cart (Reseller)" request for how multiple packages of the same product are handled. For cart_type="partner", the add is rejected with 400 if the product already has a consumer or reseller row in this buyer's cart.

Each distinct productBulkDetailsId is its own cart row — adding package #2 after already having package #1 in your cart creates a SECOND reseller row, it does not overwrite the first. Adding the same productBulkDetailsId again just increases that row's quantity. Either way, resellerMinimumQuantity/resellerMaximumQuantity bounds the TOTAL quantity across every reseller row you hold for this product (i.e. every package you've picked, counted together) — a package counts as "quantity 1" toward that cap regardless of how many units are physically inside it. productBulkDetailsId must reference an active product_bulk_details package for this exact product (see the Product Bulk Details folder).

cart_type disambiguates which of your rows for this product to update (defaults to "consumer"). For cart_type="reseller", productBulkDetailsId is REQUIRED — it identifies which specific package's row to update, since a reseller product can have more than one row (one per package). quantity sets that row's value directly (not additive); it's validated against the same consumer/reseller min-max bounds as Add To Cart, applied to the TOTAL across all of your rows for this product+type, not just this one row.

cart_type query param disambiguates which of your rows for this product to remove (defaults to "consumer"). For cart_type=reseller, productBulkDetailsId is REQUIRED — it identifies which specific package's row to remove, so removing one package doesn't wipe every reseller row you have for this product.

Returns every cart row for the buyer — one consumer row per product at most, and for reseller, one row per distinct bulk package picked (so the same product can appear multiple times as reseller rows, each with its own productBulkDetails).

request.description: Creates one pending order per cart item and returns a Stripe Checkout URL. Redirect the buyer to data.checkoutUrl. If the selected payment option has a non-zero `charges` value, it's added as a separate "Payment processing fee" line item on top of the cart subtotal.

Same endpoint as the Stripe checkout — set paymentOptionId to whichever payment_options row activates CoinPayments (name containing "crypto" or "coin payment") and pass cryptoCurrencyId (from Crypto Currencies > List) to invoice in that coin. If the selected payment option has a non-zero `charges` value, it's added as a separate "Payment processing fee" item converted at the same rate. Returns the same { checkoutUrl, sessionId } shape; redirect the buyer to data.checkoutUrl.

Same endpoint as the plain Stripe checkout above — couponCodes/addOnIds/useWallet are all optional selections/intent only. couponCodes takes one code per product (each code is matched to its own cart item and validated independently — two codes may not target the same product). The backend looks each of them up in the DB, validates eligibility (product/product type/quantity/active/validity), and computes every extra charge, add-on amount, discount, coupon discount and wallet deduction itself; nothing calculated on the client is trusted. See GET orders/checkout/pricing to preview these numbers before submitting.

request.description: Each product's isOutOfStock is true if either the admin flagged it out of stock, OR you (the requesting user) have already redeemed maximumQuantity of it — in that case purchasedQuantity/maxPurchaseReached explain why, so the frontend can hide/disable the buy button instead of showing a generic "out of stock".

Response includes currentPointsBalance and canAfford — an upfront preview of whether you have enough points, based on minimumQuantity. isOutOfStock is true if either the admin flagged it out of stock, OR you've already redeemed maximumQuantity of it (see purchasedQuantity/maxPurchaseReached) — canAfford factors this in too. The actual check happens again (authoritatively) when you call Redeem Product.

request.description: Same listing as the authenticated 'List Products' request, but no auth required. purchasedQuantity/maxPurchaseReached are always 0/false here since there's no logged-in user to scope them to.

Debits pointPrice x quantity from your PointUserBalance. maximumQuantity is a per-user lifetime cap, not just a per-request bound — this sums every purchase you've already made of this reward and rejects (400) if this request would push you over the cap, even if this individual request's quantity is within bounds. Also 400 if you don't have enough points or the product is out of stock; 404 if the product doesn't exist or isn't active.

request.description: Full referral downline tree. Each node shows earnedForMe (points earned directly from that member's own purchases) and subtreeTotal (earnedForMe + everyone below them). Response also includes a totalDownlineEarnings grand total.

Wallet snapshot, current-month earned/redeemed points, REFERRAL_LEVEL_1/REFERRAL_LEVEL_2 reward counts + totals, and trend — the last 6 calendar months (oldest first, including the current in-progress month) as [{ m, purchases, points }]: m is the month abbreviation (e.g. "Feb"), purchases is the count of this buyer's paid orders (payment_status_id = 2) that month, points is the sum of points credited to their wallet that month. Months with no activity come back as 0, not omitted, so the array is always 6 entries long.

Single merged, latest-first feed of the user's own orders, reward mall redemptions, point transactions, and teammates joining their referral network (each type tagged via the `type` field: order | reward_mall_purchase | point_transaction | teammate). Teammate entries include which level (1 = direct referral, 2 = referred by a level-1 referral), who referred them, and a live snapshot of points earned from them / their paid-order count so far. Each source is capped at its most recent 100 rows before merging, so this is a recency feed (not exhaustive history) — for full history of one source use /orders/my, /reward-mall-purchases/my, /point-transaction/my, or /users/my-team directly.

request.description: One endpoint backing the frontend's overall search bar. `type` picks a dropdown category: reseller | consumer | partner (products, gated the same way as GET /products?type=... via bulk_available/consumer_available/partner_available) | reward_mall (reward_mall_products) | referral (the caller's own direct downline, users.referral_id = caller id) | all (default — runs every category at once for a combined preview, each capped at `limit`). `q` is the keyword; omit it to just browse the category. Product/reward-mall categories match q against name, sub_title, description, information, notes, search_keywords, and each item returns { id, name, subTitle, description, category, image, sellingPrice/pointPrice }. The referral category matches q against first_name, last_name, username, unique_user_id, email and returns { id, uniqueUserId, username, firstName, lastName, fullName, email, image, status } — no product fields. Every group and item also carries `categoryLabel` (Consumer | Vimas Products | Vimas Partner | Reward Mall | Teammates) and `route` (the frontend path for that category's listing page: dashboard/mall/consumer | dashboard/mall/reseller/vimas-products | dashboard/mall/reseller/vimas-partners | dashboard/rewards | dashboard/teammates/level-1) so the frontend can redirect there directly off this response.
